findings.headline: Pay award costs create further budget pressures: NJC pay award came in at 3.3% vs 3% budgeted (£0.281m shortfall), and teachers' pay faces pressure from potential Welsh Government 3.5% proposal.
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget provided for 3% pay award for teachers from September 2026 and 3% for NJC (Green Book) staff from April 2026. The national employers' pay offer for NJC has been agreed at 3.3%. The report estimates 'there will be an in-year shortfall to the budget of around £0.281m that may need to be met from reserves if there is no compensatory grant allocation.' Welsh Government is consulting on a 3.5% teachers' award versus the 3% budgeted. While Welsh Government stated it would provide additional funding, 'updates will be provided in future reports', creating uncertainty.
findings.matters: Pay award slippage creates unbudgeted costs that may require reserve funding. The NJC shortfall is already crystallised at £0.281m; teachers' costs depend on Welsh Government funding confirmation, which is not yet secured.
findings.figures: NJC pay award 3.3% vs 3% budgeted; estimated shortfall £0.281m; teachers' potential award 3.5% vs 3% budgeted
findings.quote: The budget also provides for a 3% pay award for NJC (Green Book) employees from April 2026. The national employers pay offer of an increase of 3.3% has just been agreed. It is estimated that there will be an in-year shortfall to the budget of around £0.281m that may need to be met from reserves if there is no compensatory grant allocation.

findings.headline: School delegated budget reserves are in overall deficit of £4.798m as at March 2026, with 'significant risk' that approved redundancy budgets will be exceeded.
findings.detail: Schools' earmarked reserves show an overall deficit of £4.798m as at 31 March 2026, an adverse movement of £4.199m from March 2025. The council holds a centralised non-delegated exit costs budget to meet voluntary and compulsory redundancy costs in maintained schools. The report states: 'Due to the current level of deficit reserves held by schools, there is a significant risk that the approved budget is exceeded as specific schools work through any required redundancy processes.' This creates contingent liability exposure for the council.
findings.matters: School budget deficits suggest structural underfunding being managed through redundancies. The council faces contingent liability if school exit costs exceed the centralised budget, which appears likely given the scale and rate of deterioration in school reserves.
findings.figures: School deficit reserves £4.798m as at 31 March 2026; adverse movement £4.199m from prior year
findings.quote: In recent years there has been considerable pressure on school delegated budgets with school earmarked reserves held on 31 March 2026 equating to an overall deficit position of (£4.798m), an adverse movement of (£4.199m) from 31 March 2025 (excluding ringfenced HWB reserves). Due to the current level of deficit reserves held by schools, there is a significant risk that the approved budget is exceeded as specific schools work through any required redundancy processes.

findings.headline: A £2m Strategic Transformation Programme cost reduction target is 'currently assumed to be met in full' but detailed business cases are not due until October, creating material unvalidated savings.
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget includes a £2m cost reduction target from the Strategic Transformation Programme, based on 'a combination of existing and new projects planned for commencement in 2026/27 and is currently assumed to be met in full'. However, 'Cabinet approved some new projects in June which are now being progressed to detailed business case stage and are due to be completed in October. This will help provide a more accurate assessment of the likely cost reduction achievable compared with the target.' At Month 4, the council is assuming £2m of savings with no business case evidence.
findings.matters: Unvalidated savings of this scale represent a material risk to delivery. If these do not materialise, they will compound the existing £7.090m deficit. Deferring business case completion until October leaves two-thirds of the financial year already elapsed with no clarity on achievability.
findings.figures: £2m transformation cost reduction target; business cases due October 2026; currently 'assumed to be met in full'
findings.quote: A cost reduction target of £2m has been included in the budget which was based on a combination of existing and new projects planned for commencement in 2026/27 and is currently assumed to be met in full. Cabinet approved some new projects in June which are now being progressed to detailed business case stage and are due to be completed in October. This will help provide a more accurate assessment of the likely cost reduction achievable compared with the target.

findings.headline: Holiday pay employment tribunal claims (Brazel case) total 300+ live cases with explicit warning that final cost may be 'considerably more' than the £0.254m held in reserves.
findings.detail: Following the Supreme Court's July 2022 judgment in Harpur Trust v Brazel, holiday pay calculations for term-time and irregular-hours workers must be recalculated. Flintshire has 300+ live employment tribunal claims resulting from this. A preliminary hearing was held 5 March 2026, with case management orders through January 2027. Critically: 'There is a risk that the final cost may be considerably more than the £0.254m currently held in reserves for this purpose.' This is an unquantified contingent liability with explicit acknowledgement that the reserve is likely insufficient.
findings.matters: A contingent liability with unknown scale, and explicit warning that actual cost may substantially exceed the reserve, represents material financial risk. If final costs are multiples of the reserve, this would require additional funding and further reserve or borrowing impact.
findings.figures: 300+ live employment tribunal claims; £0.254m held in reserves; risk cost is 'considerably more' than reserve
findings.quote: The Supreme Court upheld the EAT judgment in the Brazel case in July 2022 which impacts on the calculation of holiday pay for employees who work irregular hours or for part of the year (i.e. term time). There are currently 300+ live employment claims progressing through the employment tribunal... There is a risk that the final cost may be considerably more than the £0.254m currently held in reserves for this purpose.

findings.headline: A potential waste recycling infraction fine of £1,022,386 hangs over the council if it does not meet the 70% statutory target; officers meet Welsh Government in September 2026 to determine whether it will be imposed.
findings.detail: Flintshire did not meet the statutory 70% recycling target in 2024/25. Welsh Government confirmed that previous potential infraction charges of £1.203m (for 2021/22-2023/24) have been waived, but stated 'the authority did not meet the increased statutory recycling target of 70% in 2024/25, which means that a further infraction fine of £1,022,386 could be levied'. Officers are meeting with the Welsh Government Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability in September 2026 to 'discuss the progress the authority has made to meeting the statutory target which will assist with determining the levying of the infraction charge.'
findings.matters: An infraction fine of over £1m represents a material contingent liability that could be imposed by Welsh Government and is outside the council's control. This is unbudgeted and unprovisioned, and if imposed would require further reserve drawdown.
findings.figures: Potential infraction fine £1,022,386; previous waived charges £1.203m; decision pending September 2026 meeting
findings.quote: However, the authority did not meet the increased statutory recycling target of 70% in 2024/25, which means that a further infraction fine of £1,022,386 could be levied and the authority will need to continue to demonstrate a robust and credible plan to achieving 70%. Officers are to meet with the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability in September 2026 to discuss the progress the authority has made to meeting the statutory target which will assist with determining the levying of the infraction charge.
